title: 2026 budget timetable and 5% regional levy cap
subtitle: Speed cameras in school zones, taxi accessibility, climate plan, road safety changes, Code of Conduct deferral, and contract awards.
overview: Regional Council set the direction for the 2026 budget. It approved the budget review timetable and asked staff to bring a business case for any increase that adds staff positions {{vote:m9}}. It also directed staff to draft a 2026 budget for regional services, excluding police, that limits the increase in the regional share of the tax levy to no more than 5% {{vote:m12}}. Council keeps the final say on the actual increase.

Council approved speed camera school zone changes effective May 26 {{vote:m15}} after a divided debate. It also raised the accessibility fee on taxi trips and set a larger accessible taxi fleet {{vote:m11}}. A package from the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee {{vote:m14}} covered the 2025-2030 Corporate Climate Action Plan, new pedestrian crossovers, stop signs and speed changes, a hot water heater pilot in affordable housing, and a review of last winter's maintenance.

Council deferred the updated Code of Conduct to June 25 for an Integrity Commissioner opinion {{vote:m16}}. It approved road, watermain and housing infrastructure contract spending. The Regional Chair also thanked the departing Regional Clerk. After a closed session, council returned to open session and approved the budget timetable.

decisions.detail: Council directed staff to prepare a draft 2026 budget for regional services, excluding police, that limits the increase in the regional share of the tax levy to no more than 5%, and called on federal and provincial governments for municipal stimulus funding.

Council approved the 2026 budget review timetable, sent the report to the Police Services Board and area municipalities, and required a business case for any budget increase that adds staff positions.
Council amended the Traffic and Parking By-law school zone schedules, effective May 26, 2025, in support of the Municipal Speed Camera Program.

Council raised the accessibility fee on auxiliary taxi trips from $0.07 to $0.10, increased the accessible taxi fleet from 7% to 9% with five more accessible vans in 2026, and deferred the centralized wheelchair accessible dispatch pilot.

decisions.item: Climate, traffic and winter maintenance package
decisions.detail: Council approved the 2025-2030 Corporate Climate Action Plan, a pilot converting 84 gas hot water heaters to electric in affordable housing, traffic by-law changes, and a review of Winter 2024/2025 maintenance operations.
Council increased the 2025 Children's Services operating budget by $6,775,216 with no net tax levy impact and asked the province for more Local Priorities Funding.
Council accepted the Steed and Evans Limited tender of $10,792,000 plus taxes for Phase 1 of Maple Grove Road improvements in Cambridge.
Council deferred the Code of Conduct report to June 25, 2025 to allow an Integrity Commissioner opinion on the definition of conflict of interest.

debate: A delegate told council there is a housing emergency and asked that staff work with people who have experienced homelessness to build a time-bound housing action plan by the end of 2025. Asked how this differs from the co-creators table, the delegate said that table has not moved quickly enough.

Another delegate opposed the Wilmot land assembly, citing unknown financial, environmental and democratic costs, questions about due diligence, and possible downstream liability from topsoil washing into storm drains.

On the 5% levy limit, one councillor worried it could be treated as a hard cap. Staff and others replied that staff will present a budget under 5% and council keeps discretion to go higher. Members also asked that police boards consider similar restraint.

On budget scheduling, councillors raised a conflict with a November 18 Woolwich council meeting and the burden of back-to-back budget days on members with other jobs. Staff said the dates would be adjusted and that two content sessions are meant to give time for follow-up.

On speed cameras, opponents called them a cash grab and cited 24/7 operation and low ticketing thresholds. Supporters said they change driver behaviour and that revenue goes to a road safety reserve. Staff said there is a ticketing threshold, the contract is a daily lease, and they will report on the exit clause.
On the Code of Conduct, one councillor found the conflict of interest definition too broad and worried about a low threshold for complaints, which prompted the deferral.
